sentiment: A tool you can reshape becomes a place to think; the ones you cannot are only shelves.

stories.title: Malleable software: Restoring user agency in a world of locked-down apps (2025)
stories.summary: Software that can be bent, forked, and reshaped by the person using it — a shelf of finished apps does one thing forever, but a material you can rework keeps its use open. The tool becomes a place to think rather than a thing to obey.

stories.title: Thinking fast and slow in AI: The role of metacognition (2021)
stories.summary: A mind that can watch itself think — deciding when to answer quickly and when to stop and reconsider. Reshaping a thought, not just producing one, is the part that looks most like agency.

stories.title: When did Google get so weird?
stories.summary: A tool that once felt shapeless and open now feels fixed and strange to hold. The drift is the point: systems stop bending toward their users and start bending toward themselves.
